clue.text: Till career, sights must be managed

indicators.note: letters that must be managed are handled and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A careers adviser warns that one's ambitions must be kept under control.
explanation.definitionFit: A till is the machine in a shop that records sales and holds the takings.

clue.text: Cleaner's mostly slow, and an imposter

parts.note: a char or charlady is a cleaning woman

indicators.note: mostly means the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: a slow clock is late, behind time

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is rather sluggish and turns out to be a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a fraud who claims skills or knowledge they lack, a synonym.

clue.text: Hammering, Dad's dropped off, getting hurt

indicators.note: with the father figure dropped off, those letters leave the word

parts.note: a pasting is a hammering or heavy defeat
pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: Dad nodded off during a beating and got injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dad's dropped off' reads as Dad falling asleep, but it says PA is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To sting is to hurt with a sharp smarting pain, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Direct one's attention on all but the top of hedge

indicators.note: all but the top means the first letter, at the top of a down light, is removed

parts.note: privet is a common hedging shrub

explanation.surface: A gardener concentrates on trimming everything except the top of the hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet on something is to fix one's attention on it closely, an idiom.

clue.text: Produces speed found in elements of DNA

indicators.note: found in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: genes are units made of DNA
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A biology note says that what makes speed possible lies in parts of our DNA.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to produce or create, a verb synonym in the same tense.

clue.text: Tiger seen wandering here?

indicators.note: letters wandering roam out of their original order

explanation.surface: A wildlife guide wonders if a tiger was spotted roaming in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines it as well: a vast plain where big game roams, though tigers are Asian, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is the great Tanzanian savanna famed for wandering big game.

clue.text: Push the Spanish, then submit

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
to bow is to submit or yield

explanation.surface: Shove the Spaniard aside, then give in.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow is to push or jostle someone aside, a verb synonym.

clue.text: In short, it goes far up!

definitions.text: In short, it goes far up!

parts.words: In short, it goes far up
parts.note: in short its abbreviation is RAF, which is far written upwards in a down light, and its aircraft fly high

explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation of this air arm, read upwards, spells 'far', and its planes do go far up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Britain's military air arm, whose aircraft climb high into the sky.

clue.text: Special occasions for lease-holder during shamefaced stupor, we're told (10,4)

indicators.note: during means one piece comes within the others

parts.note: someone shamefaced goes red

indicators.note: we're told means the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a daze is a stupor
a letter is one who lets out property on a lease

explanation.surface: A tenant, red-faced in a dazed state, marks the special days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts the lease-holder between the two parts; 'we're told' works only on the stupor. A letter is one who lets, so the lease-giver, a loose but common crossword reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a memorable or important occasion, once marked in red on calendars.

clue.text: Some womaniser from a sultanate

indicators.note: only some of the word womaniser is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A philanderer hailing from an Arabian sultanate.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula, and this adjective describes a person or thing belonging to it.

clue.text: August with eleven getting drunk around pub, keeling over

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters are wrapped about the other piece
the word eleven, getting drunk, staggers into a jumbled order
a word that keels over is turned upside down, so in a down-or-across reading it runs backwards

parts.note: a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A football team, all eleven players, gets drunk in a pub in August and falls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' looks like the month but is the adjective; 'keeling over' reverses the pub, which 'around' wraps the drunk eleven about.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means dignified and worthy of respect, a synonym.

clue.text: Snappy creature in what's rumoured to be back-street legwear

indicators.note: a rumour is something said, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a back street is an alley; a gaiter is a covering worn on the leg

explanation.surface: Someone asks which snapping reptile is hidden in gossip about clothing from a side street.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLEY GAITER said aloud matches the reptile's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The reptile is famous for its powerful snapping jaws, a playful description.

clue.text: Post from county town returned, having exchanged partners

indicators.note: in bridge, North and South are partners, so one compass letter swaps for its partner
returned means the town name is read backwards

parts.note: Lewes is the county town of East Sussex

explanation.surface: Mail from the county town comes back after a couple swap spouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' makes SEWEL from LEWES; 'having exchanged partners' swaps the S for N, since North and South are bridge partners. Lewes is the county town of East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the upright post at the foot or turn of a staircase.

clue.text: One's travelling unto a star

indicators.note: letters travelling move around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is journeying towards a star.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nearly defines the answer by itself: this is a space traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: One here stands for a person, specifically a space traveller trained to go beyond Earth.

clue.text: Whence Father Time surveys chieftains

definitions.meaning: the Father Time weathervane looks down from ..., the London cricket ground
rulers with power over lesser lords

explanation.surface: Old Father Time keeps watch over the tribal leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Time is a famous weathervane at Lord's, the London cricket ground, so he surveys from over Lord's.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlords are supreme rulers set above other lords, close to chieftains in sense.

clue.text: Usain Bolt ordered washing

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The sprinter Usain Bolt asked for his kit to be laundered.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablutions are the act of washing oneself, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Some 70s occasion

indicators.note: only some of the decade's name, written out in words, is kept, the outer letters dropped

parts.note: the 70s written out in words are the seventies

explanation.walkthrough: Write out '70s' as SEVENTIES; some of it, the middle stretch, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a happening or occasion, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Strike causing impasse from peer is sign of hesitation

parts.note: a peer is an equal
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An industrial stoppage creating deadlock, with a lord hesitating over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action but is a goal that levels the score, causing a deadlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal that levels the scores, leaving the match deadlocked, is a football term.

clue.text: Reach for cooker catalogue

definitions.meaning: the extent or scope something can cover
a kitchen stove with hotplates and ovens
a line or selection of products offered for sale

explanation.surface: Stretching up for a cookery catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: scope, a kitchen stove, and a product line.

clue.text: Miss one duet out of tiredness

parts.note: a miss is a girl or lass
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: out signals the word duet is put out of order

explanation.surface: A young woman gives up a duet because she is exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is weariness and lack of energy, a synonym.

clue.text: Rejected parts no longer available to a Liberal

parts.note: a dish that is off is no longer available on the menu

explanation.surface: Political cast-offs are no longer open to a Liberal politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal means the entrails and organs cut away in butchery, and more broadly refuse or waste.

clue.text: It's somewhat light or fluffy, when rising

definitions.text: It's somewhat light or fluffy, when rising

indicators.note: rising in a down light means the letters are read from the bottom up
somewhat means only part of the run of words light or fluffy is used

explanation.surface: Something airy and fluffy that rises, like foam on a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters HTORF sit inside 'light or fluffy'; 'when rising' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Froth is a light mass of bubbles that rises on a liquid.

clue.text: Time composer was in front, having seen the world

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was a French composer
to lead is to be in front, so led means was in front

explanation.surface: A composer who led the way in his era turns out to be widely journeyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-travelled person is one who has seen much of the world through journeys.

clue.text: Disorientated off shore

definitions.meaning: out on the ocean, away from land

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both confused and literally out on the ocean away from land.

clue.text: Approve mean pay-cuts, regularly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of mean pay-cuts is taken

explanation.surface: A government signs off on stingy wage reductions.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact is to pass a law or measure into force, close to approving it.

clue.text: Terribly choosy about one beginning to record second-rate singers

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the others
terribly suggests the word choosy is mangled into a jumble

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of record is taken

parts.note: B is a second-rate grade, below A

explanation.surface: A fussy producer is about to record some mediocre vocalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges CHOOSY into CHO-OYS, and 'about' places I, R and B between the O's.
explanation.definitionFit: Choirboys are boys who sing in a church choir, a specific kind of singer.

clue.text: Test arsenic, for example

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
say means for example, as in 'a fruit, say'

explanation.surface: A lab tests for arsenic, among other poisons.
explanation.definitionFit: An assay is a test of a substance to determine its composition, especially of a metal.

clue.text: Father scours around for red blood antigens

indicators.note: around signals the letters of father scours are moved about

explanation.surface: A dad scrubs about looking for traces of blood.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rh system of proteins on red blood cells determines whether blood is positive or negative.
